idiom_name: Sorbet T::Enum (enums block, singleton values, serialize)
implementation_notes: Ruby has no enum construct; the type-safe realization comes from Sorbet's T::Enum: subclass it, declare values inside `enums do ... end` as `new`, and each value is a frozen singleton instance that `is_a?` the enum class, so it cannot be passed where another type is expected. Sorbet performs exhaustiveness checking on case statements, and T::Enum provides name and serialize for boundary conversion. Plain module constants or frozen symbols - the untyped Ruby instinct - give no type-level closure at all and are not this pattern.
code_sketch:
# typed: strict
class Suit < T::Enum
  enums do
    Clubs = new
    Diamonds = new
    Hearts = new
    Spades = new
  end
end

Suit::Clubs.is_a?(Suit)    # true: a typed singleton value
Suit.deserialize('hearts') # Suit::Hearts; raises on an unknown value
pitfalls: Enum values are process-wide singletons: any state stored on them (discouraged by Sorbet) is mutated globally, and T::Enum forces instances to freeze on binding.
Without a Sorbet run there is no closure: a plain Ruby process never checks that a value belongs to the enum, so boundary parsing must still validate.
Custom serialized values must be unique across the enum - T::Enum raises at load time if two members share one.
